The PR adds a shared OpenClaw lifecycle command classifier and wires gateway-host, node-host, and direct system.run exec approval paths to require explicit approval before durable allowlist or auto-review.

PR surface: Source +2784, Tests +2162. Total +4946 across 11 files.

Reproducibility: yes. source-reproducible: current main lets the three exec approval entry points reach generic durable allowlist or auto-review decisions without an OpenClaw lifecycle mutation guard.

target.title: fix(exec): require approval for OpenClaw lifecycle commands
target.body:
﻿﻿﻿﻿Fixes #99518

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where exec commands through gateway or node hosts could let OpenClaw gateway/daemon lifecycle mutations pass through normal allowlist or auto-review paths when they should require explicit approval.

The affected workflow is OpenClaw self-management from exec surfaces: stopping, starting, restarting, running, deleting, or uninstalling the gateway/daemon through CLI, launchctl, systemctl, schtasks, process-kill, shell-wrapper, package-manager, Windows shim, `env -S`, `sudo`/`doas`, and dispatch-wrapper commands.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a focused lifecycle classifier to the exec approval policy and wires it into both gateway-host and node-host approval analysis. The guard forces explicit approval for OpenClaw lifecycle mutations unless exec is already in yolo mode (`security=full`, `ask=off`).

The follow-up update also covers foreground gateway runtime forms that were missed by the first patch: `openclaw gateway`, `openclaw gateway run`, `openclaw gateway --force`, and option-only gateway run surfaces such as `--port`. Read-only gateway inspection remains outside the guard, including `openclaw gateway status`, `openclaw gateway call ...`, `openclaw gateway --help`, `openclaw gateway run --help`, `launchctl print`, `systemctl status`, `schtasks /Query`, and generic read-only process lookups.

## User Impact

Operators get an extra human confirmation before an agent or auto-review path can stop, start, restart, run, delete, or uninstall the OpenClaw gateway/daemon in non-yolo configurations. Existing yolo-mode behavior and read-only status/query commands are unchanged.

## Evidence

Issue review feedback incorporated: lifecycle classification now has regression coverage for the ordering invariant that classification happens before durable allowlist trust or auto-review decisions.

Latest review feedback incorporated at `d6c702f501c6`: systemctl action discovery now skips value-taking options before the lifecycle verb, so `systemctl -s TERM kill openclaw-gateway.service` and `systemctl --signal=TERM kill openclaw-gateway.service` are classified before allowlist or auto-review can run. A read-only regression keeps `systemctl --type service status openclaw-gateway.service` outside the lifecycle guard.

Latest review feedback incorporated at `a7ef45f423aa`: `openclaw gateway call` is now method-aware instead of being treated as a read-only subcommand family. Lifecycle-affecting RPC calls such as `update.run` and `gateway.restart.request` require explicit lifecycle approval before durable allowlist or auto-review can run, while read-only RPCs such as `health`, `update.status`, and `logs.tail` remain outside the lifecycle guard.

Live gateway-host proof from an isolated branch gateway (`node scripts/run-node.mjs gateway run --port <random> --bind loopback --allow-unconfigured`, independent temp state/config):

```json
{
  "branchHead": "0ce214f5c1a1",
  "isolatedGateway": {
    "healthOk": true
  },
  "lifecycleAllowlistOnMissAutoReview": {
    "command": "openclaw gateway --force",
    "autoReviewCalls": 0,
    "resultStatus": "approval-unavailable",
    "hasLifecycleWarning": true,
    "warningCount": 1
  },
  "yoloFullOff": {
    "command": "openclaw gateway --force",
    "allowedWithoutPending": true,
    "warningCount": 0
  }
}
```

`approval-unavailable` is expected in this isolated proof because no approval delivery route is configured; it is still a blocking approval result before command execution, and `autoReviewCalls: 0` proves the lifecycle command was not laundered through auto-review first. The `yoloFullOff` case confirms `security=full` + `ask=off` remains unchanged.

Focused tests:

```shell
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/exec-approvals-policy.test.ts --testNamePattern="OpenClaw lifecycle|read-only or generic"
# Tests  144 passed | 111 skipped (255)

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.test.ts --testNamePattern="OpenClaw lifecycle|durable allowlist"
# Tests  5 passed | 53 skipped (58)

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-node.test.ts --testNamePattern="OpenClaw lifecycle"
# Tests  1 passed | 48 skipped (49)

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/node-host/invoke-system-run.test.ts --testNamePattern="OpenClaw lifecycle|empty env operands"
# Tests  2 passed | 33 skipped (35)
```

Static checks:

```shell
pnpm tsgo:prod
# passed

pnpm exec oxlint src/infra/exec-approvals.ts src/infra/exec-approvals-policy.test.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.test.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-node.test.ts src/node-host/invoke-system-run.test.ts src/utils/shell-argv.ts src/utils/utils-misc.test.ts
# passed

git diff --check
# passed
```

Autoreview:

```shell
python .agents\skills\autoreview\scripts\autoreview --mode local --no-web-search --prompt "Review the dirty OpenClaw PR #99530 follow-up patch..."
# attempted twice; no final clean result claimed
```

The first helper run was interrupted by an outer 3-minute timeout. The second run used `--stream-engine-output` with a 30-minute timeout, but produced no structured reviewer output and left a stuck Codex reviewer process, which was cleaned up. Focused tests, static checks, and the isolated live gateway proof above are therefore the current validation for this update.
